> Is there any reason not to apply the 1h TTL to all the cache breakpoints? Right now it's only for the system portion if I'm not mistaken. @spacepluk Src: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#pricing I personally am not willing to pay for `2x` cache write price for the messages portion of my sessions. In my setup, I have modded my OpenCode to have this status line with the cache expiry timestamp from Anthropic's server-side response and a daemon scanning all my tmux panes to find all OpenCode sessions with this timestamp and keeping my cache warm by sending `ping` messages. I pay `0.1x` price for entire context window for cache reads per ping but since leaving open sessions unattended for more than 5m is rare in my workflow, the pings rarely fire and when they do it is still cheap. Honestly, if you just have normal sessions where you are pretty much actively getting work done, paying `1.25x` for 5m works out way better than paying `2x` for the 1h marker. Yes, 1h TTL means fewer cache misses on the read side over a session's lifetime, but without a daemon keeping the cache warm you can have a session cache go stale for 1h even and then that miss costs you the full `2x` cache write anyway. That said, making it configurable for the messages markers between 5m and 1h is trivial if you need. Anthropic has made Claude Code use the `1h` markers for all of their markers including the messages portion (at least the main chat) which is overkill IMO. Everyone is paying the `2x` price unnecessarily without realizing it. I wouldn't want it for my active interactive sessions at least since I see no value in it.

Title: [Bug] Indefinite hang on startup when /tmp is mounted noexec (WSL/Hardened Linux)
Description:
On systems where /tmp is mounted with the noexec flag (common in WSL and hardened Linux environments), opencode hangs indefinitely during the initialization of the OpenTUI render library.
Behavior Analysis:
Tracing the process via strace shows that the main process and its child enter an infinite loop of thread synchronization attempts (a "futex storm"). The logs confirm that OpenTUI fails to map its native library from /tmp because of the noexec restriction:

ERROR service=default e=Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: 
Failed to open library "/tmp/.7bef6dbfdf7f5fbd-00000001.so": 
failed to map segment from shared object rejection

Instead of exiting with a fatal error, the process blocks indefinitely on an epoll_pwait2 call, waiting for an event from a native worker that never successfully initialized.
Steps to Reproduce:

   1. Mount /tmp with noexec (e.g., sudo mount -o remount,noexec /tmp).
   2. Run opencode.
   3. The process will hang silently with high CPU usage or indefinite blocking.

Workaround:
Directing temporary file extraction to a location with execution permissions resolves the issue:
export TMPDIR=~/tmp && opencode
Technical Environment:

* OS: WSL / Gentoo (defaults)
* Node Version: v24.15.0 (LTS)
* Opencode Version: 1.14.48

Suggested Fix:

* The application should detect if library mapping fails and exit with a clear error message.
* Ideally, OpenTUI should respect TMPDIR consistently or use a more standard, non-temporary path for its native binary components.

Looked into this — the root cause is exactly as described: `slash-popover.tsx` renders `cmd.trigger` (the English slash trigger like `share`, `undo`) as the primary label but never displays `cmd.title` which is properly internationalized via `language.t()`.

The fix is straightforward: display the translated title as the primary label and keep the trigger as a smaller secondary hint. Opening a PR.

My PR #26826 fixes image support at the **protocol conversion layer** in `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`, ensuring `MediaPart` is correctly transformed to `image_url` content blocks in the request body.

Noticed #21405 addresses the same file. The two fixes are complementary, not duplicates:

- #21405 fixes child vs parent `.opencode/` ordering (nested project dirs — child should win)
- This PR fixes global `~/.opencode` vs project `.opencode/` ordering (global was always winning regardless of nesting)

Both are needed for the full precedence chain to work correctly: `XDG → ~/.opencode → parent .opencode → child .opencode`.
